name: AI Chatbot for WooCommerce: Emporiqa Sales Assistant
author: Rosen Hristov

sections.description:
A shopper is on one of your product pages at eleven at night with a question you could answer in ten seconds. Nobody is at the keyboard, so she guesses, closes the tab, and you never find out what she wanted.

Emporiqa is an AI chatbot for WooCommerce that answers her itself. It works as a sales assistant and as AI customer support: it recommends products from your own synced catalog, answers pre-sale and policy questions, finds products from a photo, tracks orders, handles the objection that stalls the purchase, and walks her to checkout, in 65+ languages.

Ask the chatbot for a product you don’t sell

It says so, instead of inventing one. Product facts come from the catalog you sync, not from what the model picked up in training. When the chatbot isn’t sure, it says so and offers to bring in your team. Read unedited conversations, refusals included, on the proof page, or ask the chatbot yourself on the live demo store. That demo store sells electronics, and the behavior is the same on any catalog.

The questions a search box cannot answer

“Which size should I get?” “Do you have this in blue?” “Is this waterproof?” “Which of these two is better for a beginner?” “Can I return it if it doesn’t fit?” A search box cannot answer any of those. This ecommerce chatbot answers them from your catalog and your own policy pages, then puts the right product in the cart.

What the chatbot does with a shopper

  • Product recommendations from your catalog by what the shopper means, not by keyword match
  • Answers “too expensive” with alternatives you already sell, instead of a discount
  • Compares two products side by side, inside the chat
  • Visual search: finds the closest thing you stock from a photo the shopper uploads
  • Adds to cart and walks the shopper to checkout
  • Answers shipping, returns, and payment questions from your own synced pages
  • Hands the conversation to your team, in full, when a person is needed
  • Reports which chats ended in a purchase, with the revenue attributed to chat

A shopper types “waterproof winter boots under 80, size 9”. Your site search returns every boot you sell. This AI shopping assistant returns the four that meet all four conditions, with stock and an add-to-cart button. It works as a product finder on any WooCommerce catalog: fashion and apparel, electronics, furniture, beauty, pet supplies, sporting goods, auto parts, and B2B or wholesale ranges.

No API keys, and no second bill

You don’t open an account with an AI provider, paste a key, or watch a token meter. The AI model cost is already inside what you pay for the chatbot: $0 a month plus $0.25 per conversation, with $25 of signup credit (about 100 conversations on us) and no card required at signup. A $59/month cap is on by default and you move it from the billing dashboard. Unlimited team members, no per-seat fee. If the chatbot never talks to a shopper, you never pay. Enterprise option for catalogs over 30,000 products. Full pricing.

Setup

Install the plugin, then click Connect to Emporiqa in Settings and Emporiqa. You sign in or create a free account, pick your store, and land back in WordPress connected, with no credentials to copy between tabs. One more click sends your catalog, and the chatbot goes live on your storefront when the first product arrives. Deactivate the plugin and the chat widget is gone immediately.

Built for WooCommerce

  • All product types: simple, variable, grouped, external
  • WooCommerce HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage)
  • WPML and Polylang for multilingual stores
  • Multi-currency: WOOCS, WPML Multi-Currency, WooCommerce Payments, Aelia Currency Switcher
  • In-chat cart with stock validation, order tracking, and conversion tracking
  • 20+ filters and WP-CLI commands for developers (documentation)

The same e-commerce chatbot also runs on Drupal Commerce, Magento, PrestaShop, Shopware, and Sylius, from one account and one dashboard.

Who is behind it

Emporiqa is operated by Rosel Group LTD, a company registered in the European Union. Your shopper conversations are not used to train AI models. The plugin is built by Rosen Hristov, fifteen years building for the web and now an AI engineer, who answers pre-sales email himself.

Third-Party Service

This plugin connects to Emporiqa, an external service, in the following ways:

  • Connect handshake: When you click Connect to Emporiqa, your browser is redirected to https://emporiqa.com/connect/start for authentication. After you confirm the store on the Emporiqa side, your site receives a one-time code and exchanges it server-to-server (signed with PKCE) for a connection secret. No credentials cross the URL.
  • Webhook sync: Product and page data is sent to the Emporiqa API (https://emporiqa.com/webhooks/sync/) when content changes or during manual sync operations. Data is authenticated via HMAC-SHA256 signatures.
  • Chat widget: An external JavaScript file is loaded from https://emporiqa.com/chat/embed/ on all public-facing pages (when a Store ID is configured) to display the chatbot.
  • Shopper messages and photo uploads: What a shopper types in the chatbot, and any photo they upload for visual search, is sent to Emporiqa and processed by its AI provider to produce an answer and match it against your catalog. This content is not used to train AI models.
  • Order tracking: Emporiqa may send requests to your site’s REST API to look up order status on behalf of customers.

An Emporiqa account is required. By using this plugin you agree to the Emporiqa Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

Keeping your catalog in sync

Per-product changes (price, stock, description, images, status, trash, untrash) and product variation changes flow to Emporiqa automatically via WooCommerce action hooks. Order completions trigger the conversion webhook on woocommerce_checkout_order_processed, woocommerce_payment_complete, and the matching Store API + status-transition hooks.

Delivery is queued via Action Scheduler (bundled with WooCommerce 3.8+) with exponential backoff at 60s, 240s, and 960s, for up to 3 retries. No separate daemon is required, but WP-Cron must be functioning. If WP-Cron is disabled, set up a real cron entry hitting wp-cron.php so Action Scheduler can drain its queue.

Re-run a full sync from Settings → Emporiqa → Sync tab (or wp emporiqa sync-all via WP-CLI) when:

  • You add or change languages in Polylang or WPML. The active-languages list is auto-detected on activation and settings save, but existing products won’t carry new translations until they’re re-emitted.
  • You change the store currency in WooCommerce settings.
  • You add a new site to a WordPress Multisite install. Each site has its own settings and catalog.
  • You rename or delete a product category, brand, or attribute taxonomy term. Taxonomy events are not observed, so category names only refresh when the products using them are next re-saved.
  • You change WooCommerce tax rates or tax classes that affect displayed prices.
  • You create or modify coupons / discounts that change product pricing. Coupons themselves are not synced.
  • You import products in bulk via the WooCommerce CSV importer, WP All Import, or REST API calls that don’t fire woocommerce_update_product.
  • A custom script or another plugin writes product data directly to the database, bypassing standard product save events.
  • Emporiqa was unreachable for an extended period (network outage, planned maintenance, expired credentials). Action Scheduler drops events after 3 failed attempts, so only a manual full sync recovers them.

As a safety net, run a full sync once a week to catch any drift that may have built up from background failures.
sections.installation:
From wordpress.org (recommended):

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New in your WordPress admin
  2. Search for “Emporiqa”
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate

Manual installation:

  1. Download the plugin from wordpress.org
  2. Upload the emporiqa folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  3. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu

Setup:

  1. Go to Settings → Emporiqa in your WordPress admin
  2. Click Connect to Emporiqa. A new tab opens on emporiqa.com. Create a free account or sign in, then pick the store you want to connect (or create a new one). The plugin is connected when you return.
  3. On the Sync tab, click Send my catalog. Products and pages sync; the widget appears on your storefront when the first product arrives.

On HTTP, or prefer to paste credentials yourself? Expand Edit credentials manually on the Settings tab. Paste a Store ID and Connection Secret from your Emporiqa dashboard under Settings → Store Integration. Both flows reach the same place.

Full setup guide with screenshots: emporiqa.com/docs/woocommerce/

Integration overview: emporiqa.com/integrations/woocommerce/
sections.faq:
Can the chatbot recommend products, or does it only answer questions?

It recommends. Ask it for “a gift for a runner under 60” and it returns products you stock, with the reason it picked them, then offers to add one to the cart. AI product recommendations come from your synced catalog, including variations, stock, and price.

Does this replace the WooCommerce search box?

No, it sits alongside it. Your search box matches words; the chatbot understands a sentence with several conditions in it and answers in the shopper’s own language. Shoppers who know the product name still use search.

Can it handle customer support, or only sales?

Both. It answers shipping, returns, payment, and policy questions from the pages you sync, and it can look up an order status for a customer. When a request needs a person, such as a refund, it hands over to your team with the conversation attached.

Is this AI chatbot free?

The plugin is free, and you can install it and connect your store without a card. The Emporiqa service behind it is pay-as-you-go: $25 of signup credit (about 100 conversations on us), then $0.25 per conversation with a monthly cap you set. If the chatbot never talks to a shopper, you never pay.

Do I need an OpenAI API key or my own AI account?

No. You do not create an account with an AI provider, paste an API key, or manage tokens or usage limits. The AI model cost is already inside the per-conversation price, so there is no second bill.

How is this different from a live chat plugin?

Live chat routes a shopper to a person, so it answers when someone is at the keyboard. This chatbot answers on its own from your synced catalog, recommends products, handles objections, and only brings in your team when a person is genuinely needed. You can run both.

I don’t see Store ID or Connection Secret. Where do they come from?

You don’t need them for the one-click flow. In Settings → Emporiqa, click Connect to Emporiqa. You’ll sign in on emporiqa.com, pick a store, and the plugin receives the connection details for you. If you’d rather paste them yourself, expand Edit credentials manually on the same settings page. The Store ID and Connection Secret are in your Emporiqa dashboard under Settings → Store Integration.

Does one-click connect work on HTTP sites?

One-click connect requires HTTPS, because the connection details are exchanged through a signed handshake back to your site. If your store runs on plain HTTP, expand Edit credentials manually on the settings page and paste the Store ID and Connection Secret from your Emporiqa dashboard. Both flows land you in the same place.

Will the AI chatbot quote a product I don’t sell, or a price I changed yesterday?

Ask it for something you don’t stock and it says so, instead of inventing a product. Prices, stock, variations, and policy pages come from what your site syncs, and they update via webhooks as you change them. When the chatbot can’t answer with confidence, it tells the shopper and offers to hand off to your team. You can read unedited conversations, refusals included, on the proof page, then open the live demo and ask it yourself.

What happens when a shopper asks the chatbot something my team can’t answer at midnight?

The chatbot hands off with the full conversation attached. You can configure the handoff target in your Emporiqa dashboard (email to a team inbox, or a form the shopper fills in). The shopper isn’t left waiting on a human; they get a response right away.

How do I turn the chatbot off?

Deactivate the plugin from your WordPress Plugins screen. The chat widget disappears from your storefront immediately. Your synced products stay on the Emporiqa side until you delete the store there, so you can reactivate later without re-syncing.

What happens when the $25 credit runs out?

You’ll get an email before the credit is exhausted, and again when the next billing month’s spend approaches your $59/month default cap. If no card is on file when the credit runs out, the widget pauses on your storefront. Your store keeps working, but the chat doesn’t answer until you add a card. The cap is a hard ceiling: spending stops when you hit it, and you control whether to raise it or not from the billing dashboard.

Does the chatbot work on multilingual stores (Polylang, WPML)?

Yes. The plugin automatically detects Polylang and WPML, and syncs content in all configured languages. Languages are auto-detected on activation.

How do I do the initial sync?

After connecting, the Sync tab shows a green welcome card with a Send my catalog button. Click it to send your products and pages. Or use the Sync All button in Settings → Emporiqa → Sync tab at any time, or run wp emporiqa sync-all via WP-CLI. After the initial sync, changes are sent automatically in real-time.

Can I control which products get synced?

Yes. Use the emporiqa_should_sync_product filter:

add_filter( 'emporiqa_should_sync_product', function( $should_sync, $product ) {
    if ( $product->get_price() <= 0 ) {
        return false;
    }
    return $should_sync;
}, 10, 2 );

What post types can I sync as pages?

By default, the page post type is synced. You can configure additional public post types (posts, custom post types) in Settings → Emporiqa under “Pages and posts to include”.

Does the chatbot plugin support WooCommerce HPOS?

Yes. The plugin declares compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (Custom Order Tables).

How does order tracking work?

The plugin exposes a REST API endpoint that Emporiqa calls when a customer asks about their order. Requests are authenticated automatically using your connection secret.

Does the chatbot’s visual search work with any product?

Yes. The chatbot accepts a photo upload, describes what it sees (color, material, category, distinctive features), and searches your catalog using that description. Works best for products with photos that show the item clearly. The shopper doesn’t need special tags on your products. The visual search runs through the same catalog you already sync.

What happens if the AI chatbot says something wrong?

You can read every conversation in the dashboard, and low-rated ones are flagged automatically, so you find out from the transcript rather than from a customer complaint. Product facts follow your synced catalog, so prices and stock track your store. When the chatbot isn’t sure, it says so and offers to hand off to your team instead of guessing.

Where do the chatbot’s answers come from?

Your synced store content: products, variations, prices, stock, and the pages you choose to sync, such as shipping, returns, and FAQ. Product facts come from that catalog, not from the model’s training data. If something isn’t in what you synced, the chatbot says so rather than filling the gap.

How much does the chatbot cost?

The plugin is free. This WooCommerce chatbot is pay-as-you-go: you pay only when it talks to a shopper. $0/month base + $0.25/conversation. New accounts get $25 of signup credit (about 100 conversations on us), no card required at signup. After the credit, the monthly cap defaults to $59 and is customer-adjustable from the billing dashboard. Enterprise option for catalogs over 30,000 products. Full pricing at emporiqa.com/pricing/.
sections.changelog:
1.1.9

  • Security/Fix: a full sync that hit errors can no longer delete valid items from your Emporiqa catalog. Finalizing a sync tells Emporiqa to remove items not seen in that sync. Previously this was sent even when some batches had failed, so a transient network or server error during Bulk Sync (admin or WP-CLI) could silently wipe the affected products or pages from the chat’s index. The sync is now only finalized when every batch succeeded; otherwise you’re told to re-run it after resolving the errors. Enforced server-side, not just in the admin UI.
  • Fix: starting a “Sync All” where the pages part failed to initialize no longer finalizes the empty products sync (which would have removed the entire product catalog from Emporiqa).
  • Fix: variable products with parent-managed stock no longer over-report their quantity (a product with 4 variations sharing parent stock 5 reported 20). The shared pool is now counted once.
  • Fix: decimal quantities (stores selling by weight/measure via a decimal-quantity plugin) are no longer truncated to whole numbers in cart operations, and a product with a fractional quantity left (e.g. 0.5 kg) is no longer reported as out of stock.
  • Changed: the one-click Connect flow now requires the same administrator capability as the settings page it configures (was accessible to shop managers).
  • Compatibility: verified against WooCommerce 10.9 and WordPress 7.0.
  • No action required after upgrading.

1.1.8

  • Fix: variable products whose only sellable variations are on backorder are no longer reported as out of stock. The parent now aggregates availability with a three-state ladder (available, then backorder, then out of stock), matching the per-variation availability event so the chat never refuses a sellable variable product.
  • Fix: grouped products whose child items are all out of stock now report their real lowest price instead of 0. Price is derived from all children, not just in-stock ones.
  • Fix: a variable product’s parent now reports the lowest variation price as its headline “from” price (was an arbitrary variation). The full low-to-high range is shown by Emporiqa from the variation data.
  • Changed: removed three payload fields that the Emporiqa server does not use (price_min, price_max, prices_include_tax). The price range is derived from variations server-side; no merchant-visible change.

Older entries (1.0.0 through 1.1.7) are in changelog.txt, shipped with the plugin.
